findings.issue_text: [BUG] Destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or empty. Any booking whose event has no destinationCalendar (previously handled by the optional-chain `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` returning true) now crashes EventManager.create/all with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' during event creation, so the booking fails entirely.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` where externalCalendarId is guaranteed falsy, so find matches nothing and selectedCalendar is always undefined. When externalCalendarId is not provided, events.update is called with calendarId undefined where the old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId; the Google API rejects the request (404/400) and calendar updates for multi-host bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId silently fail.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the identical broken fallback: it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, making calendarId always undefined. Cancellation of a booking whose reference has no externalCalendarId calls events.delete with calendarId undefined; the Google API call fails and the calendar event is left behind after the booking is cancelled in Cal.com.

[BUG] createEvent returns the caller-supplied externalId (destination.externalId) unconditionally, even when the Google service fell back to `selectedCalendar || "primary"` because no destinationCalendar entry matched the credentialId. The booking reference stores externalCalendarId pointing at the destination calendar's externalId while the event was actually created on the organizer's primary calendar; subsequent updateEvent/deleteEvent calls use that wrong calendarId, hit 404, and orphan the real event on the primary calendar.

[BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a reference has a credentialId but the credential is neither in this.calendarCredentials nor found in prisma (e.g. deleted credential), `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is called with credential undefined. updateEvent calls getCalendar(undefined) which throws before the outer try/catch message replacement can produce a meaningful result, and because this happens inside a synchronous push of a call that throws immediately, the whole reschedule/update operation rejects rather than returning a per-reference failure result.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when evt.destinationCalendar is null (neither eventType nor organizerUser has one), so collective team hosts' destinationCalendars are dropped for exactly the multi-host scenario this PR claims to fix. Collective bookings created by an organizer with no destinationCalendar produce a null destinationCalendar; the team members' destination calendars are never written to and their calendars never receive the event — the primary bug this PR intends to fix persists for these hosts.

[BUG] loadUsers now throws a 500 HttpError for any non-Prisma, non-HttpError error and wraps even plain logic errors like the dynamicUserList empty check into a 400, but the catch also converts legitimate PrismaClientKnownRequestError from the user lookup into a misleading 400 'message' pass-through. A transient DB error during prisma.user.findMany (P1001 connection, P2024 timeout) is reported to the booker as a 400 client error, triggering retry storms and misclassifying outages; previously the error propagated as a 500.

[ADVISORY] The Calendar interface now requires `createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` but only the Google service in this diff consumes it; every other implementation (office365, lark, caldav, BaseCalendarService subclasses) accepts one parameter, so the credentialId contract is silently ignored by all non-Google providers. Lark/Office365/CalDAV createEvent still picks the first destinationCalendar in the array rather than the one matching the passed credential; for a collective booking with two hosts on the same provider type but different destinationCalendars, the second host's event is created on the first host's destination calendar (wrong calendar, possible permission failure) — the multi-host fix only works for Google.

[BUG] The Prisma booking create only connects `evt.destinationCalendar[0].id`, so for collective bookings the stored Booking.destinationCalendar is the first host's calendar and the other hosts' destinationCalendars from the evt array are lost. Cancellation/reminder/payment flows (handleCancelBooking, bookingReminder, stripe webhook) that read booking.destinationCalendar only ever see the first host's calendar; the other collective hosts' calendar events cannot be cleaned up or reminded, partially defeating the multi-destination model this diff introduces.

[BUG] `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` crashes with TypeError when `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array. handleNewBooking now sets destinationCalendar to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one, so `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` destructure yields undefined and reading `.integration` throws — a Google Meet booking on a host with no destination calendar fails event creation entirely.

[BUG] The `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` fallback is dead code and yields undefined whenever externalCalendarId is falsy. updateEvent called without externalCalendarId (the booking-reference-less path) sends calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update, producing a malformed API request / failed event update for every legacy booking without a stored externalCalendarId.

[BUG] deleteEvent's calendarId fallback `find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` searches for a calendar whose externalId equals the already-falsy externalCalendarId, so it always returns undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId undefined — the Google event is never deleted, leaving orphaned events on user calendars.

[BUG] The refactor drops the user.destinationCalendar fallback: bookings without a booking-level destinationCalendar now produce an empty array instead of falling back to the user's calendar. Requesting a reschedule on a booking whose destinationCalendar is null (previously handled via the user fallback the old line attempted) builds an event with destinationCalendar: [], so updateAllCalendarEvents / delete paths find no matching calendar and the organizer's calendar event is never updated for the reschedule request.

[ADVISORY] Only the first destination calendar (`evt.destinationCalendar[0]`) is persisted on the booking row, discarding all other hosts' calendars. For collective events with multiple hosts, only the organizer's calendar is stored on Booking.destinationCalendar; subsequent reschedules/cancellations reading booking.destinationCalendar (and the code paths that wrap it in a single-element array) lose every other host's destination calendar, silently degrading back to single-calendar behavior after the initial creation.

[ADVISORY] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` can push duplicates when a team member's destinationCalendar equals eventType.destinationCalendar or the organizer's, and the organizer's own team calendar is handled separately via users[0]. Collective bookings where two hosts share the same destination calendar (or the event type's calendar matches a host's) create the same calendar event twice under the same credential, leaving duplicated events hosts must clean up.

[ADVISORY] The new multi-destination createAllCalendarEvents loop, including its DB credential-fetch fallback, has no test coverage in the diff; the only test-shaped change is a playwright fixture snapshot (webhook.e2e.ts) asserting the new array shape. The core behavior of this PR — per-destination event creation, the prisma.credential.findUnique fallback for out-of-scope credentials, and the no-credentialId fan-out branch — ships with zero assertions; a regression in the credentialId mismatch path (event silently not created on a host's calendar) would go undetected until users report missing collective events.

[ADVISORY] The recurring-event deletion branch runs inside the per-reference loop, so for multi-reference bookings it iterates all user calendar credentials and deletes updated bookings' events once per calendar reference. Cancelling a recurring collective booking with N calendar references executes the same cross-credential deletion sweep N times, issuing duplicate deleteEvent calls and logging errors for already-deleted events; the branch should run once outside the reference loop.

[BUG] This PR about collective destination calendars silently inverts the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED logic in organization creation, changing which orgs get a slug vs a requestedSlug. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=true the old code suppressed slug and recorded requestedSlug; the new code sets slug directly, so billing-enabled deployments create organizations with unvetted slugs (and drop the requestedSlug metadata), a data/tenant-routing change completely untraceable to the stated intent of this PR.

[BUG] updateEvent's selectedCalendar fallback searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId, but this code only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so find() always returns undefined and selectedCalendar is always undefined. Reschedule/update of a Google booking that has no externalCalendarId stored on its reference calls calendar.events.update with calendarId: undefined, causing the Google API call to fail and the booking update to break — the intended fallback to the destination calendar never fires.

[BUG] deleteEvent's calendarId fallback uses find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy/null, so the lookup always returns undefined. Deleting a Google calendar event whose reference lacks externalCalendarId passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.delete, failing the deletion and leaving orphaned events on hosts' calendars after a booking is cancelled.

[BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents, when the DB credential lookup for reference.credentialId returns nothing, the loop variable credential remains undefined and updateEvent(credential, ...) is still called with it. A booking whose reference points to a deleted credential (exactly the case the new DB fallback exists to handle) crashes or produces a garbage result instead of being skipped or reported as failed, breaking the reschedule flow with an unhandled error.

[ADVISORY] The complete rewrite of loadUsers (new try/catch, new thrown HttpError 400/500, new guards on dynamicUserList and hosts) is a behavioral refactor of user-loading unrelated to the collective destinationCalendar fix this PR claims to implement. Dynamic-link bookings with an empty dynamicUserList that previously returned an empty user list (and failed later) now return a 400 with a different message, and Prisma known-request errors are silently coerced to 400s — future debugging of booking creation regressions will bisect to this PR whose title/description say nothing about user loading.

[ADVISORY] The booking row only stores evt.destinationCalendar[0] via Prisma connect, discarding the additional collective hosts' destination calendars that this same diff just assembled into the array. Any later code path that reconstructs the CalendarEvent from the booking (cancel, payment webhook, reminder cron) rebuilds destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar alone and drops the non-first hosts' calendars, so those follow-up flows act on a single-host view — the multi-host invariant this PR is supposed to introduce is not enforced at persistence.

[ADVISORY] The unrelated copy edits in this PR ('organiser'→'organizer' in hideCalendarNotes string and the log/comment re-indent) are mixed into a functional multi-calendar change with no requirement traceability. The organizer spelling change alters the exact additionalNotes string persisted to hosts' calendars, which breaks any consumer (tests, i18n snapshots, downstream string matchers) comparing the old value, and makes this PR's diff harder to review for the actual collective-calendar logic.

[BUG] teamMemberPromises is built from users.slice(1) unconditionally and pushes to teamDestinationCalendars via mutation inside a Promise.all map, so for a single-user (non-team) booking it's an empty array but for ROUND_ROBIN teams it now runs the map that previously was gated by users.length > 1. Round-robin events with more than one potential host will push every non-organizer host's destinationCalendar onto the evt only when schedulingType is COLLECTIVE — the guard is present, but the promise structure now always executes translation lookups for all users even when previously skipped for users.length <= 1, adding per-user translation work on every booking request with no functional need.

[BUG] The `credential` variable is declared once outside the new per-reference loop in updateAllCalendarEvents, so a failed credential lookup for one reference silently reuses the previous iteration's credential. When a booking has multiple calendar references and a reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the prisma.credential.findUnique returns null (deleted credential or team credential not owned by this user), `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` is called with the PREVIOUS reference's credential, so the calendar update for reference N is sent to reference N-1's calendar — the wrong host's calendar gets mutated and the intended one is never updated.

[BUG] In updateEvent and deleteEvent the new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares against an externalCalendarId that is by definition falsy in that branch, so find never matches and the fallback returns undefined instead of the old first-destination externalId. Any caller invoking updateEvent/deleteEvent without externalCalendarId (old bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId, which the diff itself documents as a supported legacy path) previously deleted/updated the first destinationCalendar's calendar; now the call proceeds with calendarId undefined, so the Google API is hit with an undefined calendarId and the delete/update fails, leaving orphaned events on the user's calendar.

[BUG] The legacy recurring-event deletion fan-out (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar")).map(... for (const updBooking of updatedBookings) ... deleteEvent)`) now runs once PER calendar reference because it was nested inside the new `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, and it ignores `reference` entirely. For a multi-destination collective booking with N calendar references on a recurring event, each remaining booking's event is deleted N times (one fan-out per reference), producing N×M×K duplicate Google/Lark API delete calls per cancellation — wasted API quota, rate-limit risk, and misleading apiDeletes results.

[ADVISORY] The destinationCalendar array migration only fixes Google: Lark, Office365, and the BaseCalendarService (CalDAV/Apple) still destructures only `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]`, i.e. the first element. A collective booking with multiple hosts using Lark/Office365/CalDAV still gets its calendar event written only to the first host's destination calendar — the exact bug this PR's title claims to fix — while Google users get the fixed behavior; the next contributor debugging 'works in Google, broken in Lark' tickets pays the divergence cost.

[ADVISORY] The runtime CalendarEvent model is now an array of destination calendars, but the Booking row still persists only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` via the single-relation `connect`, so team members' destination calendars are derivable only from booking references. Every path that rebuilds a CalendarEvent from the stored booking (editLocation.handler, requestReschedule.handler, deleteCredential.handler, paypal/stripe webhooks) sees only one destination calendar; any behavior that should reflect all collective hosts' destinations (e.g. BrokenIntegrationEmail, Meet fallback in EventManager that inspects destinationCalendar[0].integration) silently operates on partial data for collective bookings until the schema grows a real booking↔DestinationCalendar join table.

[ADVISORY] In createEvent the organizer's email is taken from mainHostDestinationCalendar (the first array element) while the target calendar is selected by credentialId match, so for collective events the two can disagree. When the credentialId-matched calendar is a secondary host's calendar, the event is inserted into that calendar with the organizer.email set to the first host's destination calendar externalId; Google either rejects the mismatched organizer or stores an event whose organizer doesn't own the calendar, breaking later updates/deletes keyed on organizer identity.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten expression preserves the original copy-paste bug `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar` — both operands are the same field — so the user's destinationCalendar fallback is still dropped (now yielding `[]` instead of falling back). A booking with no destinationCalendar on the booking row but one on the user gets destinationCalendar: [] on reschedule requests, whereas cancel/confirm paths fall back to booking.user.destinationCalendar; the rescheduled-then-cancelled flow can miss the user's chosen calendar.

[BUG] updateEvent's selectedCalendar fallback is dead code: when externalCalendarId is falsy, `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match, so it always evaluates to undefined. Any update path that reaches updateEvent without an externalCalendarId (the old behavior fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId) now sends calendarId: undefined to the Google API, so calendar event updates during reschedule fail where they previously succeeded.

[BUG] deleteEvent's calendarId fallback has the same dead-code defect: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` always yields undefined on the else branch. Cancellations that call deleteEvent without an externalCalendarId pass calendarId: undefined, so the Google event is never deleted and the organizer's calendar keeps events for cancelled bookings.

[BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent ignores the new credentialId-based selection entirely and always destructures the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`), and the same first-host-only logic is used in createAttendees, updateEvent, and deleteEvent. For a collective event with multiple hosts using Lark, every Lark createEvent call (one per host credential, driven by EventManager's loop) writes to host #1's calendar; the PR's stated objective — each host's event landing on their own destination calendar — silently does not hold for any non-Google provider, and hosts 2..n get no event on their calendar.

[ADVISORY] Only the first destination calendar is persisted on the booking: `destinationCalendar: evt.destinationCalendar?.length > 0 ? { connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id } } : undefined`, even though for COLLECTIVE events evt.destinationCalendar was extended with all team hosts' calendars. After creation, booking.destinationCalendar only records the organizer's calendar, so every later read of the booking (cancel, reschedule, payment webhooks all do `booking.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : ...`) reconstructs a single-element array; collective multi-host handling silently regresses to organizer-only for all post-booking operations despite the in-memory evt carrying the full list.

[ADVISORY] createEvent returns the caller-supplied `externalId` in the result unconditionally, including when the calendar service is undefined or calendar.createEvent failed and resolved to undefined. EventManager stores this result.externalId as externalCalendarId on the booking reference, so a failed calendar event creation still produces a reference row pointing at an external calendar/event that does not exist; later updates and deletes operate on phantom references instead of surfacing the failure.

[ADVISORY] The `Calendar` interface signature was changed to require `createEvent(event, credentialId)`, but only GoogleCalendarService implements the credentialId-aware behavior; Lark and Office365 implementations declare `createEvent(event)` with no second parameter. The contract change encodes Google-specific semantics into the shared interface while non-Google implementations ignore the argument, so any future caller relying on the interface's promise that credentialId selects the destination calendar gets silently wrong behavior for Lark/Office365; it also leaves the out-of-tree app-store implementations non-conforming with no migration note.

[ADVISORY] The reschedule-request evt drops the second fallback operand entirely (`bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`), where the original code (despite its duplicated typo) still had a second-operand slot that callers may have intended as user.destinationCalendar. For bookings made before a destinationCalendar was attached (legacy bookings), the reschedule-request email/event flows now carry an empty destinationCalendar array, so any downstream calendar operation triggered by the reschedule request has no target calendar where the previous code at least had the booking's value chained through a second lookup point.

[BUG] createAllCalendarEvents fetches any credential by raw id from the database with no ownership or user/tenant scoping when it is not found in this.calendarCredentials. destination.credentialId (which flows from event-type/booking destinationCalendar data) is used to prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id}}) with no filter on userId/teamId, so a credentialId that does not belong to the organizer causes the booking flow to authenticate as a different user's calendar credential and create events on that user's calendar — a cross-tenant authorization gap introduced by the new DB fallback.

[BUG] updateAllCalendarEvents' new DB fallback loads a credential by reference.credentialId with no verification that it belongs to the booking's user or team. A booking reference carrying an arbitrary credentialId (references are persisted data reachable via booking updates) makes the server fetch and use that credential's key to update/delete the corresponding calendar event, i.e. modify events on calendars the acting user does not own.

[BUG] The cancel-booking DB fallback fetches a credential purely by id with no ownership check. The previous code only used bookingToDelete.user.credentials (the owner's credentials); the new prisma.credential.findUnique({where:{id: credentialId}}) path will delete calendar events using any user's calendar credential whenever the reference's credentialId doesn't match the booking owner's credentials, enabling deletion on another tenant's calendar if a reference row's credentialId is influenced.

[ADVISORY] The user query now selects credentials: true with the prior 'Don't leak to client' comment removed, and these objects (including credential key material rows) flow toward users used in later booking/payload construction. If any of the constructed evt/user payloads are serialized to client-visible responses or logs in later steps, raw credential rows (containing OAuth refresh tokens for dynamicLinking users) leak to the browser; the removed comment indicates this was a previously tracked leak surface.

[ADVISORY] The only test modification in this diff is a fixture-literal change (destinationCalendar: null -> []) that verifies serialization shape only, not the multi-host collective behavior the PR introduces. The core behavioral change — a COLLECTIVE booking creating one calendar event per host destinationCalendar, with per-credential calendar selection in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent — ships with zero assertions anywhere in the diff; a regression that silently creates only the organizer's event or selects the wrong calendarId would pass the entire suite, and collective-booking users would find events missing from co-host calendars after booking.

[ADVISORY] The new branch that pushes teamDestinationCalendars into evt.destinationCalendar for COLLECTIVE events (including the loadUsers rewrite with new error paths and the try/catch 500 fallback) is exercised by no test in this diff; the sole test file touched (apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts, checked) covers only the BOOKING_REJECTED email payload, not booking creation. The new schedulingType: 'COLLECTIVE' gating, the users.slice(1) team-member mapping (which now also runs for single-user bookings with a different shape — firstName/lastName added), and the catch block that converts any non-HttpError into a 500 'Unable to load users' are all unverified; a mistake here (e.g. an undefined user.destinationCalendar pushed into the array) would only surface as runtime crashes in production booking flows, since no e2e or unit test creates a collective booking in this diff.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch searches destinationCalendar for an entry whose externalId equals externalCalendarId at the exact moment externalCalendarId is falsy, so find() always returns undefined and calendarId is undefined. For any booking whose stored reference lacks externalCalendarId (legacy bookings, or events created on 'primary'), calendar.events.update is called with calendarId: undefined, Google returns 400/404, and reschedules/edits of those bookings fail with no calendar update performed.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the identical dead fallback: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it always yields undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference has no externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with calendarId: undefined, the delete throws, and the calendar event is orphaned on the user's Google account while the Cal.com booking is deleted.

[BUG] createEvent echoes the caller-supplied externalId into the EventResult unconditionally, regardless of which calendar the event was actually created on (Google's `selectedCalendar || "primary"` fallback) or whether creation failed and returned undefined. When the destinationCalendar array has no entry matching the credential, Google creates the event on 'primary' but the booking reference stores destination.externalId as externalCalendarId; every later update/delete of that booking looks up the wrong calendar and 404s, leaving orphaned events and failed reschedules.

[BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a calendar reference has a credentialId that is neither in this.calendarCredentials nor found via prisma.credential.findUnique, the `credential` variable stays undefined and updateEvent(credential, ...) is still called. updateEvent passes undefined credential into getCalendar, which dereferences credential fields and throws a TypeError; the whole booking update/reschedule for that reference errors out instead of degrading gracefully.

[ADVISORY] For a COLLECTIVE team event, team member destination calendars are only appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which silently does nothing when eventType/organizer have no destinationCalendar (evt.destinationCalendar is null). Collective bookings whose organizer and event type have no destination calendar are created with destinationCalendar null/empty, so every team member's personal calendar is skipped — events silently missing from hosts' calendars with no error surfaced.

[BUG] The fallback in updateEvent is dead code: when externalCalendarId is falsy, `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` matches nothing, so calendarId is undefined where the old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. Legacy bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now get calendar.events.update called with calendarId: undefined, so the Google client rejects/fails the update (or silently targets the wrong calendar), breaking reschedule/edit of any booking created before externalCalendarId was stored.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` always yields undefined on the fallback branch. Cancelling a booking whose reference has no externalCalendarId passes calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.delete, so the calendar event is never deleted (and the delete either errors or no-ops) — the organizer's calendar keeps a ghost event for a cancelled booking.

[BUG] `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` dereferences without optional chaining, so it throws TypeError when destinationCalendar is an empty array (which this diff now produces at multiple call sites). A Google Meet booking where destinationCalendar is [] (e.g., requestReschedule always sets `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [...] : []`, and handleNewBooking sets null when neither eventType nor organizer has one) crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' instead of falling back to Cal Video, turning the reschedule/booking request into a 500.

[BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the DB lookup returns nothing (or the credential has no app slug), `credential` stays undefined and `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` is still executed. updateEvent is invoked with an undefined credential; getCalendar(undefined) rejects, and because the rejection is in a promise pushed to `result` inside the try block it is not caught by the local catch — the failure surfaces only at the caller's Promise.all or as an unhandled rejection, so reschedule fails opaquely instead of returning a per-calendar failure result like the old code's guarded path.

[BUG] The refactor inverts the slug condition: old code set `slug` only when team billing was DISABLED (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`), new code sets it only when ENABLED (`IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`). On self-hosted instances with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false, creating an organization no longer persists the slug the user chose (it lands only in metadata.requestedSlug), so the org URL/lookup by slug silently breaks after this change; conversely EE instances now write slug at creation which previously waited for verification.

[ADVISORY] The user.destinationCalendar fallback is dropped: the new code only wraps bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar and yields [] where every other handler in this diff falls back to the user's destinationCalendar. Users who rely on their personal default destination calendar get cancellation/reschedule emails and event data with destinationCalendar: [] for bookings that have no booking-level destinationCalendar, a silent behavioral divergence from handleCancelBooking/paypal-webhook/confirm.handler which all kept the user fallback.

[ADVISORY] In updateAllCalendarEvents, for each reference without a credentialId the code loops every credential of that type, so multiple references sharing the same integration type trigger duplicate updateEvent calls against the same calendars. A multi-host collective booking where old references lack credentialId issues N references × M matching credentials update calls — the same logical calendar event is updated redundantly (and with the dead-fallback bug above, against the wrong calendarId), amplifying API quota use and risking out-of-order overwrites.

[ADVISORY] teamDestinationCalendars is mutated via push inside the Promise.all mapper callback (a data-race-shaped pattern), and duplicates are not deduplicated against the organizer's calendar. Benign under current single-threaded semantics, but the next change that makes attendee resolution concurrent/I/O-parallel or adds an eventType.destinationCalendar that equals a host's personal one will produce duplicate destinationCalendar entries, causing createEvent to insert the same Google event twice for the same credential.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateEvent's fallback branch computes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` where externalCalendarId is guaranteed falsy, so find matches nothing and selectedCalendar is always undefined. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. By construction, the fallback branch runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `.find(...)` predicate compares against a falsy value and will almost always return `undefined` (destination calendars typically have a real `externalId`). This regresses from the old behavior (`: event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) which would pick the event’s destination calendar when no externalCalendarId was provided. Even without seeing the exact `calendar.events.update` callsite in the diff, the computed `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`, leading to either an invalid `calendarId` or an unintended fallback (e.g., primary), causing updates to target the wrong calendar or fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] deleteEvent has the identical broken fallback: it searches for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` inside the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, making calendarId always undefined. adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the fallback calendar id as:

```ts
externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

(and similarly in `deleteEvent`). In the falsy branch, `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, so `.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` can never match a real calendar externalId, making the fallback always `undefined`. This is a concrete logic error introduced by the diff and can prevent selecting the intended destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] createEvent returns the caller-supplied externalId (destination.externalId) unconditionally, even when the Google service fell back to `selectedCalendar || "primary"` because no destinationCalendar entry matched the credentialId. If that lookup fails (or yields a falsy/invalid `externalId`), Google will create the event on `primary`, but `EventManager` persists `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` (see `packages/core/EventManager.ts`), which would still be the caller-supplied destination externalId from `createAllCalendarEvents` (`createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Calendar interface now requires `createEvent(event, credentialId: number)` but only the Google service in this diff consumes it; every other implementation (office365, lark, caldav, BaseCalendarService subclasses) accepts one parameter, so the credentialId contract is silently ignored by all non-Google providers. adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new `deleteEvent` calendarId fallback is:

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the branch where fallback is needed), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), so it will almost always return no match and thus `calendarId` becomes `undefined` even if `event.destinationCalendar` contains a valid `externalId`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The recurring-event deletion branch runs inside the per-reference loop, so for multi-reference bookings it iterates all user calendar credentials and deletes updated bookings' events once per calendar reference. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `credential` variable is declared once outside the new per-reference loop in updateAllCalendarEvents, so a failed credential lookup for one reference silently reuses the previous iteration's credential. When a booking has multiple calendar references and a reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the prisma.credential.findUnique returns null (deleted credential or team credential not owned by this user), `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` is called with the PREVIOUS reference's credential, so the calendar update for reference N is sent to reference N-1's calendar — the wrong host's calendar gets mutated and the intended one is never updated.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.ts` within the updated `updateAllCalendarEvents` logic, `credential` is declared once outside the per-reference loop (`let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined, credential;`). Inside `for (const reference of calendarReference)`, when `reference.credentialId` is set, it assigns `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0];` and if not found tries `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)`. If that DB lookup returns null (or doesn’t set `credential`), the code still executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));` without resetting/guarding `credential`. Because `credential` is reused across iterations, a missing credential on reference N can reuse the previous iteration’s credential (reference N-1), causing the wrong calendar to be updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In updateEvent and deleteEvent the new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares against an externalCalendarId that is by definition falsy in that branch, so find never matches and the fallback returns undefined instead of the old first-destination externalId. Any caller invoking updateEvent/deleteEvent without externalCalendarId (old bookings whose reference lacks externalCalendarId, which the diff itself documents as a supported legacy path) previously deleted/updated the first destinationCalendar's calendar; now the call proceeds with calendarId undefined, so the Google API is hit with an undefined calendarId and the delete/update fails, leaving orphaned events on the user's calendar.

Previously, calls without `externalCalendarId` would still target the (single) destination calendar externalId; now they can fall back incorrectly (likely to `primary` if later code does `|| "primary"`, or pass `undefined` depending on the call site), which can break updates/deletes for legacy references and leave events orphaned on the non-primary calendar.
